title: What are JPA projections (interface, class/DTO, dynamic), and which is most performant?
keyPoints: JPA projections fetch only the columns you need instead of loading the entire entity with all its fields
Interface-based projection defines an interface with getter methods; Spring generates a proxy at runtime
DTO/class-based projection uses a JPQL constructor expression or a record – no proxy, direct object creation, fastest
Dynamic projection accepts Class<T> as a parameter, letting the caller choose the shape at runtime
DTO projection is the most performant: fewest columns, no proxy overhead, no persistence context management
Interface projection adds proxy overhead but supports SpEL @Value for computed fields
Full entity loads all columns and enters the persistence context with snapshot storage and dirty checking

s1_definition.oneliner: JPA projections fetch only the columns your API needs – interface-based uses a proxy with getter methods, DTO-based uses a constructor expression (fastest), and dynamic lets the caller choose the projection at runtime.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Interface-based projection** – define a Java interface with getter methods matching entity field names. Spring Data generates a proxy at runtime that maps only those columns from the SQL result.
- **DTO/class-based projection** – use a JPQL constructor expression `SELECT new Dto(e.field1, e.field2)` or a Java record as the return type. Direct object creation with no proxy and no persistence context entry.
- **Dynamic projection** – `<T> List<T> findByStatus(String status, Class<T> type)` lets the caller choose the projection class at runtime.
- **Performance ranking** – DTO is fastest (fewest columns, no proxy, no persistence context). Interface is second (few columns but proxy creation cost). Full entity is slowest (all columns, snapshots, dirty checking).
s1_definition.analogy: Loading the full Account entity is like the National Bank of India clerk photocopying Rajesh's entire 20-page customer file every time. Interface projection is like writing only his name and balance on a pre-printed slip. DTO projection is like printing a receipt with exactly the three fields the mobile app needs. Dynamic projection is like letting Rajesh choose which form he wants at the counter.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Full Entity:
  ┌───────────────────────────────────┐
  │  SELECT * FROM trades (20 columns)  │
  │  → Entity in persistence context    │
  │  → Snapshot stored for dirty check  │
  │  → 10MB memory for 10K rows         │
  └───────────────────────────────────┘

  Interface Projection:
  ┌───────────────────────────────────┐
  │  SELECT id, symbol, amount (3 cols) │
  │  → Spring-generated proxy object    │
  │  → NOT in persistence context       │
  │  → 500KB memory for 10K rows        │
  └───────────────────────────────────┘

  DTO Projection (fastest):
  ┌───────────────────────────────────┐
  │  SELECT id, symbol, amount (3 cols) │
  │  → Plain record/object (no proxy)   │
  │  → NOT in persistence context       │
  │  → 300KB memory for 10K rows        │
  └───────────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
JPA projections fetch only the columns your API needs, dramatically reducing data transfer, memory, and CPU. Interface projections declare getter methods in an interface – Spring generates a proxy. They uniquely support SpEL `@Value` for computed fields like `getDisplayName()`. DTO projections use a JPQL constructor expression or a record – no proxy, direct object creation, and the fastest approach.

At National Bank of India, the Trade entity has 12 columns including large TEXT fields for notes and audit history. The trade listing API needs only tradeId, symbol, and amount. Rajesh uses DTO projection `TradeOverview(tradeId, symbol, amount)` which fetches 3 columns instead of 12 – 85% less data transferred. For 10,000 trades: full entity loads 120,000 field values plus 10,000 snapshots. DTO loads 30,000 field values with zero snapshots.

Always prefer DTO projections for read-only API endpoints. Use interface projections for quick prototyping or when you need SpEL computed fields. Use full entities only when you need to modify the data, because dirty checking requires the entity in the persistence context.

Remember one sentence: DTO projections fetch only what you need, skip the persistence context entirely, and are the fastest way to read data through JPA.
